summary: Built a small Python sample showing an onboarding orchestrator that models applications as Beanie documents in Azure DocumentDB. The orchestrator runs three simple agents (ID verification, risk assessment, account opening) sequentially, applying each state transition atomically using Motor sessions/transactions and appending an embedded history. Project includes a seed script, index-creation script, a CLI entrypoint, a FastAPI surface, and unit tests (mocked) that run without a live cluster. I verified dependency installation, seeded the live cluster, ran an orchestrator run that updated one application document, created indexes via Motor, inspected documents and indexes using the documentdb MCP tools, and ran pytest (1 passed).
how_to_run: 1) Copy .env.example -> .env and set DOCUMENTDB_URI (and optionally DOCUMENTDB_DB). 2) Create and activate a virtualenv. 3) pip install -r requirements.txt. 4) python scripts/seed.py (seeds three sample applications). 5) python scripts/run_cli.py --app-id applicant-1 (runs the orchestrator for the sample applicant). 6) Optionally run the FastAPI server: uvicorn sample_orchestrator.api:app --reload (ensure PYTHONPATH includes src or run through scripts/run_cli-like wrapper). 7) Run tests: pytest.
verification_done: load_skill calls: documentdb-data-modeling, documentdb-driver, documentdb-indexing loaded successfully.
pip install -r requirements.txt: succeeded (packages installed: beanie==1.25.0, motor==3.1.1, fastapi==0.98.0, etc.).
scripts/seed.py: executed, output 'Seeded sample applications' (3 sample docs upserted into sample_banking_15.onboarding_applications).

python scripts/run_cli.py --app-id applicant-1: executed; orchestrator ran the three agents sequentially and updated the document; final state was ACCOUNT_OPENED; sample transitions printed to console.
documentdb_find_documents (MCP): returned sample documents including applicant-1 with state ACCOUNT_OPENED and embedded history (verified persisted transitions).
scripts/create_indexes.py: executed and created indexes (idx_state and idx_applicant_state) via Motor create_index calls.
documentdb_list_indexes (MCP): showed _id index plus idx_state and idx_applicant_state among indexes on onboarding_applications.
not_verified: documentdb_create_index MCP tool: attempted earlier and failed (function returned an error). Workaround used: created indexes with scripts/create_indexes.py via Motor; the motor-based creation was successful and verified via documentdb_list_indexes. Evidence: documentdb_create_index returned errors on two attempts; recorded as tool failure.

LLM/agent integration using LangChain or a real LLM provider: the sample includes a placeholder dependency (langchain) and deterministic in-process agent functions for id_verification, risk_assessment, and account_opening. Real LLM calls were not executed or integrated (no provider credentials used) and thus LLM-based agent behavior is not verified.

Vector or full-text index usage: this sample demonstrates simple single-field/compound indexes. It does not create or verify vector or cosmosSearch-based indexes (those require additional parameters and a choice of embedding model/dimensions). The readiness report guidance for vector indexes was followed (do not create naive vector indexes) but vector index creation was not implemented.
End-to-end API tests: the FastAPI app was added but not load-tested or exercised through HTTP in automated verification (the core orchestrator CLI run and unit tests were executed instead).
open_issues: documentdb_create_index MCP tool failed when attempted; I created indexes using Motor as a workaround and verified via documentdb_list_indexes. The MCP create_index failure should be investigated if MCP index creation is required in other workflows.

The sample uses deterministic in-process agent implementations for clarity. If you want real LLM-driven agents, update agents.py to call your LLM provider (set OPENAI_API_KEY or Azure credentials) and implement prompt/response handling. The repository includes langchain in requirements.txt as a placeholder.

Beanie/Driver versions: I selected beanie==1.25.0 and motor==3.1.1. If you upgrade beanie/motor in future, verify the initialization patterns and the Settings API since Beanie has had breaking changes across 1.x and 2.x milestones.
